description: HydroSHEDS is a suite of continuous global hydrographic layers: core grids of conditioned elevation, flow direction and flow accumulation, and derived vector products including HydroRIVERS, a line network of 8.5 million river reaches (35.9 million km) with length, river order and an estimate of long-term discharge, HydroBASINS, one million sub-basins nested in 12 Pfafstetter levels for up- and downstream analysis, and HydroLAKES, all co-registered by shared IDs. World Wildlife Fund US started the project in 2006; version 1 was derived mainly from SRTM at 3 arc-seconds (with coarser HYDRO1k data above 60 degrees north), and version 2, from TanDEM-X at 1 arc-second, is released for the Americas. Coverage is global. The layers are a free download as geodatabases, shapefiles and grids, for scientific, educational and commercial use under the HydroSHEDS licence agreement with attribution. Caveats: it does not reach the accuracy of local high-resolution river and catchment maps, and attributes on HydroRIVERS and HydroBASINS are mostly geometric. Simulation uses: river and catchment topology for routing flows to and from dams, intakes and wastewater outfalls, and for flood and drought exposure. Related records: HydroWASTE (data-hydrowaste), which is co-registered to HydroRIVERS, and GRanD (data-grand-global-reservoir-and-dam-database).
